title: Span rehydration/backfill toolkit: reconstruct missing spans from logs & metrics
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Some production services intermittently drop span emission (e.g., sudden SDK failures, network partitioning, or client sampling misconfiguration). These gaps hurt end-to-end latency and error investigations and inflate SLO burn because Tempo/Jaeger traces lack critical spans.

Goal: Build a reusable Span Rehydration / Backfill Toolkit that can: (1) detect candidate missing spans by correlating traces, structured logs, and metrics; (2) reconstruct approximate spans (parent/child relationships, timestamps, attributes) with explicit provenance metadata; and (3) safely inject them into our trace backends (OTLP -> Tempo/Jaeger) as backfilled events, while preserving ordering guarantees, deduplication, and auditability.

Approach/Constraints:
- Input signals: existing partial traces (OTLP), structured logs (JSON logs with trace/span hints), request/response metrics (latency histograms), and audit events.
- Reconstruction policy: prefer exact spans if present in logs (trace_id/span_id present). Otherwise synthesize spans with deterministic IDs, include "rehydrated":true and a provenance tag (source:logs|metrics|heuristic).
- Ingestion: backfill pipeline writes via our OTLP gateway with a distinct tenant/backfill label and a write-mode header to avoid conflation with original spans. Backend will accept these but mark them as backfilled for queries and retention.
- Safety: 1) deduplication window (30m by default) using idempotency keys; 2) rate limit backfill writes per-tenant to avoid bursts; 3) admin opt-in per project for automatic backfills (opt-out default).
- Observability: produce metrics (backfills_attempted, backfills_success, dedup_rate, avg_rehydrate_latency) and tracing for the backfill job itself.

Tradeoffs discussed:
- Fidelity vs. noise: synthesized spans can confuse downstream tooling (alerts, latency SLOs). We mitigate by making queries and dashboards filterable by provenance and by excluding backfilled spans from SLO calculations unless explicitly opted-in.
- Complexity: building a fully accurate reconstruction engine is high-cost. MVP targets 3 common patterns (http server spans, db client spans, queue consumer spans) and exposes hooks for service teams to add heuristics.

Non-goals: full semantic reconstruction of application stack; automatic SLO rewrites.

Design & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Span+Rehydration+Design (internal); prototype notebook with heuristics: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/rehydration-proto; initial schema spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/blob/main/trace-rehydration/README.md

Rollout plan: alpha run in staging -> opt-in beta for 3 internal services (ingest, frontend, payments) -> collect impact -> gradual tenant opt-ins.

Acceptance criteria are below.
acceptance_criteria: Detect missing-span candidates from partial traces + logs with >90% precision on labeled staging dataset
Rehydration pipeline can emit reconstructed spans to OTLP with a backfill provenance attribute and idempotency key
Backfilled spans are excluded from default SLO dashboards and queries unless 'include_backfilled=true' is set
Rate limiting and per-tenant burst controls throttle backfill writes; stress tests show no backend overload at 5x expected load
Operational metrics and a dashboard exist for backfill attempts, success/failure, deduplication, and latency
Security review signed-off (data flow, PII in logs, encryption) and KMS usage audited
tasks: Spec the minimal rehydration schema and OTLP envelope markers
Implement log->span extractor (pattern rules + JSON path config)
Build rehydration worker: candidate detector, synthesizer, idempotency key generator
Add OTLP write-mode header + tenant backfill label support in trace gateway
Instrument metrics and create Grafana dashboard and alerting rules
Run staging dataset evaluation and generate labeled precision/recall report
Prepare rollout opt-in config and docs for service owners
Security review and threat model update
comments: 2026-03-01 - Miguel Torres: Spiked a proof-of-concept extractor using fluentd filter; initial heuristics detect ~92% of missing http-server spans on staging dataset. Need to harden idempotency key format.

2026-03-02 - Aisha Kaur: Design review notes: ensure backfilled spans carry explicit metadata 'backfill.provenance' and 'backfill.source_time' timezone-normalized UTC. Add requirement to redact PII from reconstructed attributes. Security review requested.

2026-03-03 - Emma Li (Reviewer): Concern about query blow-up in Tempo when many synthesized spans are added. Recommend a default retention TTL of 7 days for backfilled spans and a flag to archive older backfills to cold storage.
2026-03-04 - Miguel Torres: Implemented idempotency using SHA256(trace_id||parent_hint||span_name||source_ts) and tested replay prevention across worker restarts. Draft PR opened: see links.
2026-03-05 - Samir Patel (Platform): We should expose a safe-mode switch in the console to pause automated backfills per-org. I'll add a small API and RBAC check to the gateway.
